description: A* finds a cheapest path from a start state to a goal. It always expands the open state with the lowest `f = g + h`: `g` is the cost of the best path found to the state, and `h` estimates the remaining cost to the goal. If `h` never overestimates (it is *admissible*), the first path to a goal that A* expands is optimal. A better estimate means fewer expansions; with `h = 0`, A* is Dijkstra's algorithm.

papers.authors: Peter E. Hart, Nils J. Nilsson, Bertram Raphael
papers.title: A Formal Basis for the Heuristic Determination of Minimum Cost Paths
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
